title.en: On the board: Importance and limitations

narration.en: Why control? Six reasons on the left; four limits on the right.

say.en: Why control? Six reasons on the left; four limits on the right.
It helps achieve goals, checks if standards are realistic, and saves resources.
It motivates staff, keeps order and discipline, and aids coordination.
But morale is hard to measure, outside factors can't be controlled, people resist, and control costs money.
Rule: control only where its benefit is greater than its cost.

narration.en: Sort each statement: importance of controlling, or limitation of controlling.

explanation.en: Controlling helps reach goals, check standards, use resources well, motivate and keep order; but it is limited by hard-to-measure standards, external factors, resistance and cost.

text.en: Helps the firm reach its goals
Shows whether standards were set right
Workers know how they will be judged, so they try harder
Employee morale is hard to measure in numbers
The firm cannot control a new government policy
Workers resent CCTV cameras on the shop floor
A costly control system for a tiny shop may cost more than it saves

body.en: It is difficult to set quantitative standards for things like job satisfaction or employee morale. A firm has little control over external factors such as government policy, technology changes or competition. Employees often resist control, for example CCTV cameras. And control is costly in time, effort and money, so its benefits must exceed its cost.
body.kn: ಗುಣಾತ್ಮಕ ವಿಷಯಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕ ಮಾನದಂಡ ನಿಗದಿ ಕಷ್ಟ; ಬಾಹ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಕಡಿಮೆ; ನೌಕರರ ವಿರೋಧ; ಮತ್ತು ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ವೆಚ್ಚದಾಯಕ.

problem.en: A small shop with sales of ₹3 lakh a year is advised to install an inventory-tracking system costing ₹2 lakh a year. Should it, and which limitation applies?

steps.en: The control system would cost two-thirds of the shop's entire annual sales.
Control is worth it only when its benefits exceed its cost.
Here the cost is far too high for a small firm.

answer.en: No; controlling is a costly affair, and small firms may not afford elaborate systems.
